summary: AE + SE walked through Redwood Hosted API for chat and text generation: streaming responses, key generation parameters, retry behavior, SDK examples, and a short Console tour. Customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated for latency-sensitive scoring; primary concerns: latency/tail, cost, data residency, and integration with internal SSO/KMS. Agreed next steps to share pricing, run a benchmark deep dive, and exchange prompt set.
transcript:
Header: 2026-06-30 15:00 PDT — Duration approx 42 mins
Attendees: Ethan Park (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Luis Ortega (Redwood Solutions) — Claire Donovan (Southport Finance, Head of ML), Marcus Lee (CTO), Sara Patel (SRE), Omar Khan (Product)

Intro / 00:00:00 — Ethan: okay hi everyone thanks for joining, we'll keep to 40ish minutes, quick intro, i'm Ethan Park, AE at Redwood, with Maya our SE and Luis from solutions. can you all quick intros?
00:00:12 — Claire: hey Claire here, Head of ML at Southport, we run credit scoring and customer support ai, mostly internal microservices calling models for scoring, latency matters, cost matters.
00:00:20 — Marcus: Marcus CTO — curious about hosted api throughput and if we can hit p95 < 200ms for short prompts.
00:00:27 — Sara: Sara — SRE, i'll ask about VPC/network and encryption.
00:00:31 — Maya: quick agenda: hosted API basics, demo of chat & text endpoints, streaming, param tuning, retries, then console quick tour and q&a.

Demo start / 00:01:05 — Maya: so first, the hosted API — simple REST/SDK; for chat we show messages arrays, system/user roles, streaming for lower latency. i'll share my screen. (link: https://redwood.ai/quickstart) 
00:01:39 — Maya: code sample, python, from redwood import Client — client.chat.create(...). here's how you set streaming: stream=True, you'll get chunked events and can show partial tokens. this reduces TTFB.
00:02:05 — Marcus: so streaming is server-sent events? what's the client lib using under the hood?
00:02:12 — Maya: yes SSE or websocket depending on sdk — python uses chunked http and yields. node has ws support. caveat: depending on proxies, SSE may buffer; we also provide a websocket SDK for lower buffering.
00:02:35 — Claire: do you support response delta tokens? we need to show progressive scoring to downstream systems.
00:02:42 — Maya: yes you get deltas, partial tokens, each event has token and meta, also you can receive chunk with role/content. small transcription note: sometimes transcript says "deltas" as "delters" — ha.

Parameters / 00:03:10 — Maya: moving to generation params — temperature, top_p, max_tokens, presence/ frequency penalties, stop sequences. set temperature 0.0 for deterministic scoring, 0.2-0.8 for more creative. top_p complements temperature.
00:03:38 — Claire: for scoring we plan to use temperature 0 and top_p 1 to keep deterministic. what's the best practice for stop sequences when scoring?
00:03:47 — Maya: for scoring you often include an explicit separator token, and set max_tokens small, and stop sequence to ensure model doesn't hallucinate trailing. also use logprobs for token-level scoring if needed.
00:04:08 — Omar: how about prompt caching or prefix caching? we've got a lot of repeated context.
00:04:14 — Maya: Redwood supports prefix/KV caching on the runtime layer — automatic when you reuse conversation ids or pass kv cache hints, reduces token compute. good for chatbots and scoring with shared context.

Retries & idempotency / 00:04:50 — Maya: retry behavior — HOSTED API by default is polite on retries: idempotency keys for requests where you need at-most-once. for streaming partials, clients should detect truncated streams and retry with same idempotency key. we show code: headers{"Idempotency-Key": uuid4()} and server will dedupe.
00:05:20 — Marcus: does retry change cost? if a retry replays tokens we might double-charge.
00:05:25 — Ethan: good Q — we bill per token generated successfully; a retry that completes will be billed for the tokens produced; if retry produces duplicates we can help minimize by supporting byte-range resume for some models and we recommend tight timeouts + idempotency keys.
00:05:45 — Claire: and backoff? exponential?
00:05:48 — Maya: yes sdk has built-in exponential jitter backoff; defaults are conservative, you can tune in client config.

Console tour / 00:06:20 — Luis: switching to Console — usage dashboard, per-route latency breakdown, token-cost views, trace links to individual requests. quick tip: enable streaming debug to see raw SSE chunks. (link: https://console.redwood.ai)
00:06:48 — Claire: can we see request/response logs? debug logs are available but obfuscated for pii by default, we can enable full logs under a retention/access policy.
00:07:02 — Maya: yes logs are RBAC gated, audit trails in enterprise plans. note often transcript says "RBAC" as "R-BAC".

Security / 00:07:30 — Sara: our infra requires SSO, SAML, KMS integration and we need SOC2 evidence. what's supported?
00:07:37 — Ethan: we support SSO/SAML, role-based access, customer-managed KMS for Private deployments and dedicated can be integrated with your KMS in many cases. hosted keeps keys managed unless you choose Bring-Your-Own-Key for certain plans; we provide SOC2 Type II and ISO docs (link to security pack).
00:08:05 — Sara: data residency — our compliance team may require EU data to stay in region.
00:08:09 — Maya: hosted supports regional endpoints; you can pin region for data residency. for strict residency or on-prem we recommend Redwood Private deployment.

Performance discussion / 00:08:40 — Marcus: earlier you mentioned p95 latency; what's realistic for small prompts (<=64 tokens) on hosted?
00:08:49 — Maya: typical p50 30-80ms for optimized models, p95 depends on queue/batching — around 120-250ms for small prompts on our verified fast configs. using streaming reduces TTFB. dedicated gives more predictable p95 with reserved GPU pools.
00:09:10 — Marcus: how's batching handled? will it hurt latency if we enable batching aggressively?
00:09:17 — Maya: it's workload-aware — runtime does continuous batching with latency SLOs. you can set target max-latency or use Dedicated for strict SLOs. optimization settings in Redwood Optimize suggest batching config per endpoint.

SDK examples / 00:09:50 — Maya: quick code: node example shows creating chat, streaming, handling reconnects with idempotency. python snippet:
00:10:00 — Speaker 2: "with client.chat.stream(... ) as stream: for event in stream: if event.type=='delta': print(event.delta)" (note: speaker labels may be generic in transcript)
00:10:20 — Claire: do you have prebuilt wrappers for our go microservices?
00:10:24 — Luis: we have REST + gRPC coming soon; current libs are python/node/java unofficial community lib. gRPC roadmap is next quarter.

Cost discussion / 00:10:45 — Marcus: our cost target is $0.0006 per token for scoring at scale; how do we measure unit economics?
00:10:55 — Ethan: Console has token-level cost breakdown, and Optimize suggests quantization/model variants for cost. you can route lower criticality requests to cheaper quantized variants. caching also reduces billable tokens.
00:11:20 — Claire: can we do A/B between different model variants easily?
00:11:24 — Maya: yes rollouts in Console — canary, A/B with traffic weights, auto fallback policies.

Technical deep dive teaser / 00:11:40 — Maya: if you want deeper perf numbers we'll run a benchmark: share prompt set, desired p95, and we'll run a dedicated tuning with latency profiles and show kernel/quantization suggestions.
00:11:55 — Marcus: yes let's plan that.

Common objections & answers / 00:12:05 — Claire: concern about hallucination in scoring — do you provide structured output or function calling?
00:12:12 — Maya: hosted supports structured output via json schema enforcement and function/tool calling to reduce hallucination; you can validate model output server-side.
00:12:30 — Omar: retries & duplicate outputs again — our pipeline dedupes but we want idempotence guarantees.
00:12:36 — Ethan: re-iterating idempotency-key usage and server dedupe for supported endpoints.

Live demo continued / 00:13:10 — Maya: i'll send a live chat demo, streaming on — (streaming starts) you can see partial tokens appearing at 00:13:18, TTFB ~ 45ms in demo env. small glitch in caption: steamer vs streamer in auto text.
00:13:45 — Marcus: that's good. what's sample rate?
00:13:49 — Maya: depends on model and sdk, you can tune chunk size at client side for smoother display.

Edge cases / 00:14:30 — Sara: network interruptions — what happens if stream drops?
00:14:35 — Maya: client sdk will surface truncated flag; you can retry with same idempotency key and the backend will resume in many cases, or replay; for strict exactly-once, we advise durable caching in your sidecar.

Integration notes / 00:15:05 — Luis: many customers embed Redwood behind an internal inference proxy for routing, metrics, auth. our API works fine behind proxies but watch SSE buffering. websocket option is better behind some proxies.

Pricing ask / 00:15:40 — Marcus: are there volume discounts or reserved pricing?
00:15:44 — Ethan: yes hosted has tiered volume discounts; Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly/annual commits, and Private is enterprise licensing. we'll send pricing sheet after call.

Questions from customer / 00:16:10 — Claire: curious about model catalog — do you host open models and redwood-curated variants?
00:16:17 — Maya: yes model catalog with verified performance profiles; we host open models and provide quantized variants. we also publish recommended kernels/quantization for workloads.
00:16:35 — Omar: can we bring our own model?
00:16:38 — Ethan: in Private/dedicated you can deploy your model; Hosted supports custom model onboarding via enterprise channels.

Operational tooling / 00:17:00 — Maya: Console has per-route dashboards, tracing hooks to link requests to logs, and alerts for quality/regression via Redwood Optimize.
00:17:15 — Claire: how do quality regressions surfacing work? we want to catch prompt drift.
00:17:20 — Maya: you can attach evals/prompt sets and get regression alerts tied to recent commits or model rollouts.

Wrap-up / 00:17:55 — Ethan: quick recap: we'll send pricing, security pack, quickstart repo. Maya will schedule benchmark deep-dive. Claire to send prompts and SLOs.
00:18:10 — Claire: sounds good.

(Noise / 00:18:20 — small crosstalk, someone on background)

Closing QA / 00:20:00 — Marcus: one more — does Redwood support partial token logprobs with streaming?
00:20:07 — Maya: yes logprobs can be streamed but be aware of extra compute; useful for scoring and calibration.

Late-minute details / 00:21:00 — Sara: network egress concerns — will data leave region for hosted?
00:21:07 — Ethan: region pinned endpoints keep processing in the region; we can provide data flow diagrams for compliance.

Final recap (end of call) / 00:22:00 — Ethan: action items recap: pricing + quickstart, benchmark deep-dive, prompt set. schedule follow-up next week. thanks all.

Notes: transcript contains occasional mis-transcriptions (proper names, acronyms). Shared artifacts: pricing sheet (link shared in chat), quickstart repo (https://github.com/redwood-inference/quickstart), security pack (link), console demo recording (link to recording).
